extracted.intended_audience: journal peer reviewers of clinical manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journal reviewers on evaluating clinical research manuscripts, emphasizing clinical relevance, ethics, reporting standards, and practical applicability for clinicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic peer review principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic peer review principles apply to all manuscript types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standard reviewer responsibilities (e.g., fairness, confidentiality, timeliness, constructive feedback) when assessing a clinical manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial assessment — skim for content/objectives; evaluate novelty in methodology or conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a quick skim to understand the manuscript's aims and scope and to judge whether the methods or conclusions offer novel insights worthy of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Target audience focus — work must address a clinical problem (not just a research question) and use practitioner-appropriate language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the manuscript is framed around a clinical problem relevant to practitioners and whether terminology, explanations, and recommendations are accessible to a clinical audience rather than being purely research‑centric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural clarity — clearly organized and easy to understand for busy clinicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess organization, flow, and clarity: the manuscript should be well-structured with clear headings and concise presentation so clinicians can rapidly grasp key findings and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical applicability — emphasize implementation potential; include clinically applicable screening tools where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the extent to which findings can be implemented in clinical practice; look for practical recommendations, usable screening or assessment tools, and discussion of barriers to implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case study evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Case study evaluation — only essential information, patient privacy protected, no over-generalized conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For case reports/series, ensure only clinically necessary details are reported, identifying information is removed or consent documented, and conclusions are appropriately cautious given the limited data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict-of-interest disclosure — verify authors disclose all potential conflicts including ghostwriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that author declarations include financial and non-financial conflicts, funding sources, and any use of professional writers or ghostwriting; flag missing or unclear disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical participant protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical participant protection — confirm a statement of ethical standards exists, even when research was exempted from informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for ethics committee/IRB approval statements, informed consent statements or documented exemptions, and adherence to ethical standards for human participant protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical trial standards — proper recruitment, ethical procedures, randomization, statistical analysis, EQUATOR network compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess trial methods for appropriate recruitment and enrollment, ethical conduct, randomization and allocation concealment, adequate statistical analysis, and adherence to reporting standards (e.g., CONSORT or other EQUATOR guidelines).
